text_note.zh: 语料本“鸾刀”作“銮刀”，这里按通行本作“鸾刀”。
text_note.en: The corpus writes luán dāo (carving knife) with a different character for luán; the common text's form is used here.

readings.zh: “衣裳”在古诗里读 yī cháng，指上衣和下裙。口语里读 yī shang。
readings.en: In old poems yī cháng means upper garment and skirt and is read cháng. In everyday speech it is yī shang.
Chèn shēn means the clothes fit well, so it is read chèn.

readings.zh: “厌饫”是吃得太饱、吃腻了，读 yàn yù。
readings.en: Yàn yù means stuffed and tired of food, read yàn yù.
Lǚ qiē means cutting into fine shreds, so it is read qiē.

readings.zh: “宾从”指宾客和随从。今天一般读 cóng，旧时“随从”的“从”读 zòng。
readings.en: Bīn cóng means guests and attendants. Today it is usually read cóng; in older usage this meaning was read zòng.

readings.zh: “杂遝”读 zá tà，形容人多杂乱。
readings.en: Zá tà is read this way and means a busy, mixed crowd.
Chéng xiàng, the chancellor, is read xiàng.

glosses.zh: 三月三日：上巳节，古代春天的节日，人们到水边游玩，洗去不祥。
glosses.en: sān yuè sān rì: the third day of the third month, the Shangsi Festival, when people went to the waterside to play and wash away bad luck.

glosses.zh: 长安水边：指长安城东南的曲江池，是游春的好地方。
glosses.en: Cháng'ān shuǐ biān: the waterside of Chang'an, meaning Qujiang Pool in the southeast of the city, a favorite spring spot.

glosses.zh: 丽人：美丽的女子。
glosses.en: lì rén: beautiful women.

glosses.zh: 态浓意远：姿态艳丽，神情高傲，不容易亲近。
glosses.en: tài nóng yì yuǎn: showy in looks, proud and distant in manner.

glosses.zh: 淑且真：看上去又贤淑又端庄。
glosses.en: shū qiě zhēn: looking gentle and proper.

glosses.zh: 肌理细腻：皮肤细嫩光滑。
glosses.en: jī lǐ xì nì: smooth, fine skin.

glosses.zh: 骨肉匀：身材匀称，不胖不瘦。
glosses.en: gǔ ròu yún: well-proportioned, neither fat nor thin.

glosses.zh: 绣罗：绣了花的丝绸。
glosses.en: xiù luó: embroidered silk.

glosses.zh: 照暮春：在晚春的阳光下闪闪发亮。
glosses.en: zhào mù chūn: shining in the late spring light.

glosses.zh: 蹙金：用金线绣出花纹，金线绣得密密的。
glosses.en: cù jīn: patterns sewn tightly with gold thread.

glosses.zh: 麒麟：传说中的吉祥神兽。
glosses.en: qí lín: the qilin, a lucky beast of legend.

glosses.zh: 翠微㔩叶：用翠玉做成的薄薄的花叶形首饰。㔩叶，古代妇女的一种头饰。
glosses.en: cuì wēi è yè: thin leaf-shaped hair ornaments of green jade. È yè was a kind of woman's head ornament.

glosses.zh: 鬓唇：鬓角边上。
glosses.en: bìn chún: the edge of the hair at the temples.

glosses.zh: 腰衱：裙带，或腰后的衣襟。
glosses.en: yāo jié: the skirt sash, or the back of the waist.

glosses.zh: 稳称身：服服帖帖，非常合身。
glosses.en: wěn chèn shēn: sitting smooth and fitting perfectly.

glosses.zh: 就中：其中。
glosses.en: jiù zhōng: among them.

glosses.zh: 云幕：画着云彩的华丽帐幕。
glosses.en: yún mù: rich curtains painted with clouds.

glosses.zh: 椒房亲：皇后、贵妃的亲戚。椒房，汉代皇后住的宫殿，墙上涂了花椒和泥，这里指杨贵妃。
glosses.en: jiāo fáng qīn: relatives of the empress or consort. The Pepper Room was the empress's hall in Han times, its walls plastered with pepper and clay; here it means Consort Yang.

glosses.zh: 虢与秦：虢国夫人和秦国夫人，都是杨贵妃的姐姐。
glosses.en: Guó yǔ Qín: the Lady of Guo and the Lady of Qin, both elder sisters of Consort Yang.

glosses.zh: 紫驼之峰：紫色骆驼的驼峰，是很珍贵的菜。
glosses.en: zǐ tuó zhī fēng: the hump of a purple camel, a rare dish.

glosses.zh: 翠釜：翠绿色的精美锅子。
glosses.en: cuì fǔ: a fine green pot.

glosses.zh: 水精：水晶。
glosses.en: shuǐ jīng: crystal.

glosses.zh: 行素鳞：端上来白色的鱼。素鳞，白鳞的鱼。
glosses.en: xíng sù lín: serving white fish. Sù lín means white-scaled fish.

glosses.zh: 犀箸：用犀牛角做的筷子。
glosses.en: xī zhù: chopsticks made of rhinoceros horn.

glosses.zh: 厌饫：吃腻了，吃得太饱。
glosses.en: yàn yù: stuffed and tired of rich food.

glosses.zh: 鸾刀：刀环上挂着小铃的刀，用来切肉。
glosses.en: luán dāo: a carving knife with little bells on its ring.

glosses.zh: 缕切：切成细丝。
glosses.en: lǚ qiē: cut into fine shreds.

glosses.zh: 空纷纶：白白地忙个不停。
glosses.en: kōng fēn lún: busy for nothing.

glosses.zh: 黄门：宫中的太监。
glosses.en: huáng mén: palace eunuchs.

glosses.zh: 飞鞚：骑马飞奔。鞚，马笼头。
glosses.en: fēi kòng: galloping on horseback. Kòng is a horse's bridle.

glosses.zh: 不动尘：骑得又快又稳，连尘土都不扬起。
glosses.en: bù dòng chén: riding so fast and smooth that no dust rises.

glosses.zh: 络绎：一个接一个，不断。
glosses.en: luò yì: one after another without end.

glosses.zh: 八珍：各种珍贵的美食。
glosses.en: bā zhēn: all kinds of rare delicacies.

glosses.zh: 哀吟：音乐声婉转动人。
glosses.en: āi yín: music so moving it seems to sigh.

glosses.zh: 杂遝：人多，乱哄哄的。
glosses.en: zá tà: crowded and bustling.

glosses.zh: 实要津：占满了重要的位置。要津，重要的渡口，比喻重要的官职。
glosses.en: shí yào jīn: filling all the key posts. Yào jīn means an important ferry crossing, a picture for powerful offices.

glosses.zh: 逡巡：慢悠悠的样子，这里形容很神气、不慌不忙。
glosses.en: qūn xún: slow and unhurried; here, grand and self-assured.

glosses.zh: 当轩：对着车门或帐门。
glosses.en: dāng xuān: right at the carriage door or tent entrance.

glosses.zh: 锦茵：锦缎做的地毯。
glosses.en: jǐn yīn: a brocade carpet.

glosses.zh: 杨花：柳絮。
glosses.en: yáng huā: willow fluff.

glosses.zh: 白苹：水面上开白花的浮草。
glosses.en: bái píng: a floating water plant with white flowers.

glosses.zh: 青鸟：神话里替西王母传信的鸟，后来指给情人传信的使者。
glosses.en: qīng niǎo: the blue bird that carried messages for the Queen Mother of the West in myth; later, a go-between for lovers.

glosses.zh: 炙手可热：手一靠近就觉得烫，比喻权势极大。
glosses.en: zhì shǒu kě rè: so hot it burns your hand, meaning power so great that people fear it.

glosses.zh: 绝伦：没有谁能比。
glosses.en: jué lún: beyond compare.

glosses.zh: 慎莫近前：千万别走近。
glosses.en: shèn mò jìn qián: be careful not to go near.

glosses.zh: 丞相嗔：丞相会发火。丞相指杨国忠，杨贵妃的堂兄。嗔，生气。
glosses.en: chéng xiàng chēn: the chancellor will get angry. The chancellor is Yang Guozhong, Consort Yang's cousin. Chēn means to be angry.

translation.zh: 三月初三，天气清新，
translation.en: On the third day of the third month, the air is fresh;

translation.zh: 长安城的水边，来了很多美人。
translation.en: by the waters of Chang'an there are many fair ladies.

translation.zh: 她们姿态艳丽，神情高傲，看上去贤淑端庄，
translation.en: Showy and proud, they look gentle and proper;

translation.zh: 皮肤细嫩，身材匀称。
translation.en: their skin is smooth, their figures just right.

translation.zh: 绣花的丝绸衣裙，在晚春里闪闪发光，
translation.en: Their embroidered silks shine in the late spring,

translation.zh: 上面用金线绣着孔雀，用银线绣着麒麟。
translation.en: with peacocks in gold thread and qilin in silver.

translation.zh: 她们头上戴着什么？
translation.en: What do they wear on their heads?

translation.zh: 翠玉做的花叶首饰，一直垂到鬓边。
translation.en: Green jade leaf ornaments hanging down by their temples.

translation.zh: 从背后看又是什么样子？
translation.en: What do you see from behind?

translation.zh: 缀着珍珠的裙带压在腰间，十分合身。
translation.en: Pearl-weighted sashes at the waist, fitting perfectly.

translation.zh: 其中云纹帐幕里的，是贵妃的亲戚，
translation.en: Among them, behind cloud-painted curtains, are the Consort's kin,

translation.zh: 皇帝赐给她们大国的封号：虢国夫人和秦国夫人。
translation.en: given titles of great states by the emperor: the Ladies of Guo and Qin.

translation.zh: 翠绿的锅里端出紫色的驼峰，
translation.en: From green pots come purple camel humps;

translation.zh: 水晶盘子里盛着白色的鱼。
translation.en: on crystal plates, white fish are served.

translation.zh: 她们吃腻了，拿着犀角筷子很久都不下筷，
translation.en: Tired of rich food, they hold their rhino-horn chopsticks and do not eat;

translation.zh: 厨师用鸾刀切成细丝，白白地忙个不停。
translation.en: the cooks slice with bell-hung knives, busy for nothing.

translation.zh: 太监骑马飞奔，连尘土都不扬起，
translation.en: Eunuchs gallop in so smoothly that no dust rises,

translation.zh: 从御厨里一趟趟送来各种山珍海味。
translation.en: bringing one rare dish after another from the palace kitchen.

translation.zh: 箫鼓声婉转动听，连鬼神都被感动，
translation.en: Flutes and drums play so movingly that even spirits are stirred;

translation.zh: 宾客随从挤满一地，都是占着要职的人。
translation.en: guests and attendants crowd around, all holding powerful posts.

translation.zh: 后来骑马的人慢悠悠的，多么神气，
translation.en: The last rider comes slowly, so grand and sure,

translation.zh: 到了帐门前下马，走上锦缎地毯。
translation.en: gets off at the entrance and steps onto the brocade carpet.

translation.zh: 柳絮像雪一样落下，盖住了白苹，
translation.en: Willow fluff falls like snow and covers the white water plants;

translation.zh: 青鸟飞走，嘴里衔着一条红手巾。
translation.en: a blue bird flies off with a red kerchief in its beak.

translation.zh: 他权势大得烫手，没有人能比，
translation.en: His power is so hot it burns, beyond compare;

translation.zh: 千万别走近，丞相会发火的！
translation.en: take care not to go near, or the chancellor will be angry!

background.zh: 这首诗一般认为写于唐玄宗天宝十二载（753年）春天。那时杨贵妃最受宠，她的堂兄杨国忠当上了宰相，她的姐姐们被封为韩国、虢国、秦国夫人，一家人权势很大，生活奢侈。三月三日上巳节，长安人都到曲江边游春，杨家兄妹也来了，排场非常大。杜甫看到这些，写下了这首诗。
background.en: This poem is usually dated to the spring of 753, under Emperor Xuanzong. At that time Consort Yang was the emperor's favorite. Her cousin Yang Guozhong had become chancellor, and her sisters were made the Ladies of Han, Guo and Qin. The family had great power and lived in luxury. On the Shangsi Festival, the third day of the third month, the people of Chang'an went to Qujiang Pool for a spring outing. The Yang family came too, with a huge show of wealth. Du Fu saw it and wrote this poem.

author_note.zh: 杜甫（712—770），唐代大诗人，被称为“诗圣”。写这首诗时，他在长安住了好几年，还没有得到官职，生活清苦。他看到了权贵的奢侈，也看到了百姓的贫穷。几年后，安史之乱爆发，杨家也随之倒台。
author_note.en: Du Fu (712–770) was a great Tang poet, called the Sage of Poetry. When he wrote this poem, he had lived in Chang'an for several years without an official post, and he was poor. He saw both the luxury of the powerful and the poverty of ordinary people. A few years later the An Lushan Rebellion broke out, and the Yang family fell with it.

appreciation.zh: 这首诗像一部讽刺的“纪录片”。杜甫一句批评的话都没说，只是把看到的东西一样一样摆出来：美人的皮肤、衣服上的金孔雀、头上的翠玉、腰间的珍珠；锅里的驼峰、盘里的鱼，吃腻了都不想动筷子；太监骑马不停地送菜，乐声震天，随从挤满一地。最后，真正的大人物杨国忠慢悠悠地来了，大家都不敢靠近。“杨花”“青鸟”两句，历来多认为是在暗讽杨国忠和虢国夫人关系不正当。写得越华丽，越让人觉得不对劲。最后一句“慎莫近前丞相嗔”，像在小声提醒，冷冷的，又让人害怕。
appreciation.en: This poem is like a mocking documentary. Du Fu never says one word of blame. He just sets out what he sees, one thing at a time: the ladies' skin, the gold peacocks on their clothes, the jade in their hair, the pearls at their waists; camel hump in the pots, fish on the plates, food so rich they will not lift their chopsticks; eunuchs riding in with dish after dish, loud music, a crowd of attendants. At last the real big man, Yang Guozhong, arrives slowly, and no one dares go near. The lines about willow fluff and the blue bird have long been read as a quiet jab at an improper closeness between Yang Guozhong and the Lady of Guo. The more splendid the picture, the more something feels wrong. The last line, "take care not to go near, or the chancellor will be angry", is like a whispered warning, cold and a little frightening.
